Evan —

Thanks for the clear notes and the annotated file. I've looped in Redwood legal and product (laura, rishi, ben) to get a consolidated response. High level proposal from our side:

1) Output ownership (Section 5.2) — we can confirm that VentureGrid retains ownership of Customer Content and final outputs that are direct verbatim deliverables (reports, extracted data files). For generated content that is derivative or depends on Redwood system prompts/augmentation, we propose a license-to-use model where VentureGrid receives a perpetual, royalty-free right to use and sublicense outputs for their products, while Redwood retains rights to internal improvements.

2) Training / Feedback license (Section 7) — Redwood can offer an opt-out: by default, sample-level telemetry/aggregate feedback may be used to improve models, but any use of VentureGrid-origin data for model re-training will require express opt-in (order form checkbox or schedule). If VentureGrid opts in, we can agree to narrow scoped usage: training only on de-identified, aggregated data and excluding sensitive PII categories.

3) Carveouts — for regulated datasets (PHI, regulated financial customer lists), we will provide an explicit exclusion and not use for training even with opt-in.

I've attached our internal redline (VentureGrid_MSA_redline_v3.pdf) that shows the suggested language so you can compare line-by-line. If that looks acceptable, we can prepare a clean order form with the opt-in checkbox for training and an exhibit that documents the output license terms.

Proposed next steps: legal-to-legal markups this week; commercial finalize order form and signature routing next week. Does that timeline work for you?

Thanks,

Soojin / Ben —

Thanks for the context. Quick summary of recommended markups:

A) Output ownership (Section 5.2) — Proposed clause: "Customer retains ownership of Customer Content and any Deliverables that are literal reproductions or direct extractions of Customer Content. For Derivative Outputs (outputs that materially transform or synthesize Customer Content combined with Redwood system content), Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, non-exclusive, transferable, royalty-free license to use such Derivative Outputs in Customer products, provided Customer does not incorporate Redwood Confidential Models as a redistributable artifact."

We add a definition section: ""Direct Outputs": outputs that are literal or near-literal reproductions of submitted Customer Content. "Derivative Outputs": outputs that result from transformation of Customer Content combined with Redwood model processing."

B) Training / Feedback license (Section 7) — Two options in the clause:
- Default: "Redwood will not use Customer Content or Direct Outputs for model re-training. Redwood may collect anonymized telemetry and aggregate usage statistics for service quality improvements."
- Opt-in schedule (Order Form Exhibit): "If Customer opts in via the Order Form, Redwood may use de-identified, aggregated Customer data for model training subject to exclusions listed in Exhibit A (e.g., PHI, payment card data, specified proprietary datasets). Redwood agrees to maintain records of datasets used for training and will provide attestations upon request under NDA."

C) Additional protections — include an exhibit listing excluded categories and a requirement for Redwood to provide a Data Use Report quarterly if Customer opts in. Also propose a short SLA paragraph that if model regressions attributable to Customer data occur, Redwood will prioritize mitigation.

We are comfortable with the license language above; it's commercially reasonable and protects both parties. Please confirm if Ben wants any pricing/discount tie to the opt-in option. If not, we can send redline back to VentureGrid legal tomorrow morning.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
